Before you begin

  • Check with your doctor before starting any new exercise routine.
  • Keep a sturdy, non-wheeled chair nearby for balance and seated exercises.
  • Stop right away if you feel pain, dizziness, or shortness of breath.
  • Keep a glass of water within reach and take breaks whenever you need one.

Exercise library

Every move below can be done at home with no special equipment. Each one has its own moving demonstration and a link to a video.

Missing an exercise?

Tell us which exercise you'd like to see here. The site owner reads every suggestion.

Move together, remember together

Gentle, playful exercises designed for a grandparent and a grandchild to do side by side. Safe for older joints, fun enough for a six-year-old.

Grandparents & Grandchildren

Each activity has a role for the grown-up and a role for the child, and its own moving picture of that exact activity. An adult should always supervise.

My Workouts

Personal plans built around your week. Open one to see your calendar.

Eight weeks, one goal

The twelve-week programme follows the shape of the Otago Exercise Programme — leg strength and balance, three times a week, with walking in between — which is the combination the published evidence links to fewer falls. It is not the official programme and this app is not a physiotherapist: if you have already fallen, or feel unsteady, be assessed by one first.

A plan is a week. A programme is a destination: something you cannot do today and should be able to do in two months. Three sessions a week, each one a little harder than the last.

Health AI — your movement helper

Tell it what hurts, or tell it what you'd like to improve — stronger legs, better posture, more visible muscles, more energy. It asks a few questions back, then suggests exercises, including brand-new ones built for you.

This is not medical advice. It's a guide built from general rehabilitation and training principles. It cannot examine you or make a diagnosis. Always check with your doctor or physiotherapist before starting, especially after a fall, surgery or a new injury.

Tip: mention where it hurts, when it hurts, and how long it's been going on.

Your reported injuries

Saved to your account so your suggestions and plans can take them into account.

How is the pain today?

One tap a day. After a few weeks the line tells you something no single day can: whether this is getting better. The days you trained are marked underneath.

Two checks your physiotherapist would do

These are the same two timed checks used in clinics to see how steady you are on your feet. Do them once a month. They take under a minute, and the number going down over the months is worth more than any single result.

Have a sturdy chair against a wall and somebody nearby the first time. If you feel dizzy or unsafe, stop — that in itself is worth telling your doctor.

Stand up five times

Sit with your arms crossed on your chest. Stand up fully and sit down five times, as quickly as you safely can. Press start, then stop the moment you sit down the fifth time.

0.0 s

Get up and walk three metres

From sitting: stand, walk three metres at your normal pace, turn, come back and sit down. Use your stick or frame if you normally do. Press start as you rise, stop as you sit.

0.0 s

These numbers are a guide, not a diagnosis. Take them to your doctor or physiotherapist — they are exactly the kind of thing that is useful in a consultation.

Add by hand

No web page can read the step counter while it is closed — that is a rule of the phone, not a missing feature. Leave this page open (walk mode keeps it awake on a dark screen) and every step is counted, with or without internet.

Two minutes around the house

Half of preventing a fall has nothing to do with exercise. These are the things every set of clinical guidelines asks about — most of them cost nothing to fix, and a loose rug has ended more independent lives than any missed workout.

A card for the fridge

One page with your name, who to call, your doctor, your medicines and the emergency number for your country. Print it and put it on the fridge — that is the first place an ambulance crew looks.

People you can call

For a son or a daughter

Your mother has not fallen yet

One person in three over sixty-five falls each year. Most of them were managing perfectly well the week before. What changes the odds is not walking more — it is leg strength and balance, three times a week, kept up for months. That is the whole of what this does.

She does not have to learn anything

You set it up once, on her telephone, in about five minutes. After that it is one big orange button, a voice that tells her what to do, and a drawing of each movement. No typing, no menus, no passwords to remember.

You can see, without asking

Once a week you get a short note: how many times she trained, for how long, her run of days, her steps. Nothing else — no health notes, no messages. She agrees to it once and can take it back whenever she likes.

And you can be in it with her

Exercise together at the same time, each in your own house, watching each other\'s timer. Video call the whole family at once. The grandchildren have their own set of things to do with her.

Built for the body she has

Every exercise can be done sitting. Anything that hurts is swapped for something that does not, permanently. If she writes that something is wrong, it tells her plainly when to stop and see a doctor instead.

How you set it up for her

  1. Choose a plan below and pay — on your own telephone, with your own card.
  2. You get a family code. Open the site on her telephone, sign her in, and enter the code once.
  3. Press "Put this on my home screen" so it sits next to her photographs, not inside a browser.
  4. Add yourself as her friend, and ask her to choose you for the weekly note.

Two honest things. This is exercise, not medicine: it lowers the chances of a fall, it does not remove them, and anybody who has already fallen or feels unsteady should be seen by a physiotherapist first. And half of falls prevention is not exercise at all — it is a loose rug, a dark corridor and the right slippers. There is a two-minute list for that inside, free, whether or not you ever pay us anything.

Groups

Settings

Language

Menus, buttons, exercises and instructions are all translated.

Voice announcements

Read each exercise name aloud during guided sessions.

Your earned discount

Reach the day\'s step goal, or finish a full week of a programme, and you earn ten per cent off — once. It is spent on the first plan you use it on, and it does not work on the bonus pack.

What you have agreed to share

Every time you let somebody see your numbers — and every time you take that back — it is written down here with the date. Nothing about your health leaves this device without one of these lines.

Exercises you set aside

Anything you marked as not for you. They are never put in a session again — unless you allow one back.

Let me know

A message or a call reaches you even when this page is behind another window. The telephone buzzes either way; the written notice needs your permission once.

Blocked people

Nothing from them reaches you — no messages, no requests, no ringing. They are never told, and you can undo it here.

Size of everything

Not only the words: buttons, timers and drawings grow with the text, so nothing ends up too small to press. Ctrl and + or − does the same from a keyboard.

Colours

A dark screen is kinder at night; the high contrast setting uses pure black and yellow, which is what people with poor sight can read most easily.

Big words on screen

Everything the voice says also appears in large letters at the bottom of the screen — for anybody who does not hear it well, or has the sound off.

How much the voice says

From silence, to just the name of each exercise, to a coach who talks you through it.

Speaking speed

Slower is easier to follow across a room.

Try the voice control

Turns the microphone on for twenty seconds and writes down everything it hears, so you can see for yourself which words work. Nothing is recorded or sent anywhere.

Voice control

During a guided session, listen through the microphone so you can say "next" or "pause" instead of reaching for the screen.

Reduce motion

Turn off timer animation and moving demonstrations.

Comfort Assist

If we notice you increasing text size or re-reading a screen often, gently suggest larger text and simpler layout.

        Content protection

        No website can truly disable a screenshot — the operating system owns that key. What this does: blocks printing and PDF export, blocks copying and dragging the content, blanks the screen the moment a capture shortcut is pressed, and stamps every screen with the viewer's name and ID so a leaked picture can be traced back.

        Sign in with Google (real accounts)

        Paste an OAuth Client ID here and the sign-in screen shows Google's own button, with real Google accounts. Leave it empty and the built-in account chooser is used instead.

        1. Go to console.cloud.google.com → APIs & Services → Credentials → Create credentials → OAuth client ID.
        2. Application type: Web application.
        3. Under Authorised JavaScript origins add exactly:
        4. Copy the Client ID (it ends in .apps.googleusercontent.com) and paste it below.

        Friend requests between devices
        
        
        A web page cannot post a request to somebody else’s phone on its own — it needs one shared address to leave it at. A free Firebase Realtime Database gives you that in about three minutes, and no card is asked for.
        
        
          
          
        1. Go to console.firebase.google.com → Add project (any name) → skip Analytics.
          2. 
          
        2. In the left menu: Build → Realtime Database → Create database → choose a region → start in test mode.
          3. 
          
        3. Copy the address at the top — it looks like https://your-project-default-rtdb.firebaseio.com — and paste it below.
          4. 
          
        4. Press Test. Then, in Rules, paste this so only the friends area stays open:
          { "rules": { "ss": { ".read": true, ".write": true } } }
          5.

        Payment guard (this is the important one)
        
        
        Without this, a padlock is only good manners: anyone can add ?unlock=yearly to the address and walk in. The file stripe-worker.js next to this page is a small free server that Stripe tells about every payment, in private. Put it up (its instructions are at the bottom of that file), paste its address here, and the app stops believing the address bar.
        
        
        
        
        
        
        
        
        
        
        
        
        Payments & ownership
        
        
        Who is selling — required on invoices and by law
        
        
        Selling to consumers in the EU means the trader has to be identifiable: a name, a postal address, an email, and a VAT number if you have one. This is printed on the terms page and shown next to the price.
        
        
        
        
        
        
        
        
        
        
        Leave this empty and no address is shown anywhere. Your administrator email is never printed on the site: it is the one that opens this panel, and publishing it invites people to try it.
        
        
        Guided tour
        
        
        The tour on the front page is drawn by the app and needs nothing. If you ever record a real video of the site, paste its embed address here (YouTube: Share → Embed → the src address) and it plays as the first chapter instead.
        
        
        
        
        Clinical review
        
        
        If a physiotherapist has read through the exercise library, put their name, registration number and the date here. It is shown at the top of the Exercises page. Leave it empty rather than write something that is not true — this is the one field where a fib would be genuinely dangerous.
        
        
        
          
        
          
        
          
        
        
        
        
        
        
        
        
        
        
        
        
        
        
        
        
        
        
        
        
        
          
        
          
        
        
        
        
        
        
        Return links to paste into Stripe
        
        
        In each Stripe Payment Link, open After payment → Redirect customers to a page you choose and paste the matching link below. Access only switches on when the customer comes back through one of these.
        
        
        
        
        
        Saved.
        
        
        How the money reaches you.Every purchase now goes through Stripe's own checkout page: the customer types their card there, and the money lands in the Stripe account that owns the Payment Links above. This page never sees a card number and never unlocks anything on its own. The one honest limitation of a site with no server: the unlock happens because Stripe sends the customer back to your return link, which a determined person could type by hand. When you are ready for airtight verification, add a small backend that listens to Stripe webhooks.
